notes:
Put recurring work on the clock, and keep every self-improvement loop on a leash.

## Scenes worth trying

### "Run the backup script every night at 23:00. I don't want to keep a chat open."

The scheduled-tasks card now holds mechanical work, not just model prompts. Point a task at a script, a plan step, another session, an email, a ring, or a mix of these run in order. Choose a fixed cycle, a random window, a one-off moment, a delay, or a condition such as "when this file appears". Each task carries its own approved scope: the script content, arguments, working folder, or the mail account and recipients. Later runs stay inside that scope, and changing the scope asks you again.

### "My laptop was asleep at 9:00. Tell me, and let me decide."

A missed task produces one system message, even if several tasks were missed while you were away. Open it to see each missed moment grouped by task. Run the selected one now, skip it, or type what you want in your own words; WArmy turns your text into a proposal you confirm before anything runs. The rest of the schedule keeps going. A task linked to a plan step shows in both cards and executes once.

### "Mail the finished report to the client every Friday at 17:00."

Add your SMTP account when you create the task. WArmy asks for the server, port, sender, recipients and content source at setup, and keeps the password in the operating system's protected storage. A test send goes only to a recipient you name and confirm. The receipt tells you the server accepted the message; delivery still depends on the mail service.

### "When we build software together, keep the work cheap and checked."

Development mode is a per-session switch in the chat menu. With it on, the workhorse works in small batches, keeps mechanical checks fast, and stops retrying the same failing diagnosis after two attempts — it reads the real error or asks you instead. When it notices you are creating a program, it offers the switch and explains the trade-off; it never turns itself on. The session's own development habits improve from your feedback, checked against a held-out set of your past tasks before they apply, and you can pause the automatic tuning at any time. A suggestion to restructure your project waits for the next conversation and asks for your decision, with the pros, cons, risks and a rollback plan. Nothing moves without your agreement.

## Also in this release

- Self-drive now pauses itself after 3 consecutive proposals without a reply, and unchecks its own menu item. Re-check it whenever you want the workhorse to resume nudging. The count is consecutive, not a lifetime total.
- The project files card marks the most recently changed file with a clock icon: theme color when the change happened in the latest conversation round, text color when the last change was in an earlier round. Viewing a file never counts as a change.
- Diwen, the machine-verifiable concept layer, is updated to 6.15.2 (218,419 concepts) and built in. Deterministic knowledge — evolution guards, self-improvement elements, prediction notes — can now carry a Diwen sidecar for drift-free machine exchange. Your original text is always kept: disabling Diwen hides the sidecar and everything reads as before; re-enabling converts the rest in idle batches.
- Background summarization now judges its own workload before running and reviews the outcome afterwards, shrinking its batch when it runs long and growing it when there is headroom. Foreground use always wins.
- A governance layer now watches every self-improvement loop in the app (routing prediction, ETA, evolution guards, self-drive quality, development rules, workload, Diwen conversion). Proposals that touch safety or stop improving are refused silently. Proposals that change what is improvable, or what "better" means, ask for your approval first and run only after you agree. Improving the improvement method itself is allowed, but nesting beyond three levels is automatically consolidated.
- The desktop companion's read-aloud and recording recover correctly when another app takes the microphone or speaker mid-task.
- Reduced-motion settings now truly stop the sweeping animations.
- The workhorse detail dialog keeps its start/stop and delete controls.
- All new screens and messages ship in the 27 interface languages.

## Honest boundaries

- A scheduled external effect (a sent mail, a script's side effect) cannot be promised exactly-once across crashes and sleep; WArmy records what it knows and asks you about the rest.
- Development-mode and governance improvements are conditional on the evidence collected in your sessions. They are not a guarantee of better results on every future task.
- Model output still needs your review. Permissions stay per session, and no self-improvement can disable the safety boundaries.

## Verification

The changed surface passed 3 consecutive targeted acceptance rounds with 0 failures (13 gates per round: self-drive consecutive cap, artifact recency icon, Diwen 6.15.2 batch conversion with disable/re-enable, workload judgment, governance hard/soft gates and nesting merge, plus syntax/privacy/i18n/card-structure/performance regressions). The 96-gate baseline suite passed 3 consecutive rounds earlier. A 60-pair foreground/background performance regression kept foreground p95 within the 5% tolerance (measured +1.3% total, +1.0% first-token with development mode on).

## Install

Download WArmy-Setup-0.4.48.exe from this release and run it. Choose a folder, launch WArmy, and your existing WArmyData carries over. The installer is unsigned; Windows SmartScreen may ask for confirmation. SHA-256 hashes are listed in checksums.txt. First run stops at the language page and waits for you.
